notes.title: SMALL UPDATE
notes.notes:
-Enemy bases now take damage on a basis of how the game now calculate shrapnel, so a bomb going off a few meters away will not contribute much of any damage, whereas ANY overlapping explosion spheres would contribute 50% damage. So this will make blowing up bases more difficult, direct hits or explosives detonated INSIDE bases are your best bet at destroying them quickly!
-Enemy bases now show a cracked/damaged exterior as they incur damage!
-Enemies can now see you through windows, so they will attempt to shoot through glass if they see you behind the window. This should've been in the game a long time ago.

notes.title: SMALL UPDATE: OFF HAND PISTOL GRIPPING
notes.notes: Got tired of my off hand floating where a shooter would have theirs pulled up against the other hand to brace against recoil. It isn't setup where the hand assumes a pre-determined pose, but rather will "freeze" in place when held up against the other hand, allowing the player to then grip and curl their fingers closed like they're actually off-hand gripping the pistol. It looks much better than before.

notes.title: MAJOR UPDATE: M16 INTERACTIONS!
notes.notes:
Any gun bro will absolutely eviscerate a poorly constructed gun in a video game. That said, they will still certainly tear into the ones in this game, but today, I got the m16 a major step closer to functioning like the real thing. 

Now, you can pull back and release the bolt on the M16 to cycle rounds! Before, you could only close the breech when it was open to chamber a round. 

There are still bugs, and I am learning how to iron them out so this can be 100% complete and functioning, so expect some jank.

notes.title: GAMEPLAY UPDATE: RANDOMIZED ENEMY BASE AND AMMO CACHE LOCATIONS
notes.notes:
The game has been feeling a bit too predictable, with enemy bases spawning in fixed locations that never changed. This led to spawned enemies taking the same paths time and time again. To fix this, I added a set of several random location the enemy bases can spawn from. 

This adds some subtle variety. For example, when the game starts and enemy bases spawn, they can end up closer or farther to the players begin location, either giving them extra time to prepare, or forcing them to scramble to protect themselves from incoming baddies. 

This also applies to the armory, you'll need to search around the map for it, as it now also spawns in a few random places. 

To help you spot the armory, it has been colored neon orange to make it easier to see at a distance.

notes.title: VR CONTROLLER/HAND ADJUSTMENT UPDATE!
notes.notes:
After waaaay too long, I have finally implemented a solution for altering player VR hands relative to their motion controllers. Now, you can set your own offsets using the easy to use system. Just touch the link sphere with your right-hand controller, then using your OTHER controller, touch the axis coordinate arrows to move/rotate the controller of your right hand. You can toggle between positive or negative location or rotation adjustments, then you can hit save. If you don't like your changes, just touch "reset" to return the hands to their default position I programmed relative to my own Valve Index controllers. If you play with knuckle controllers, you should be all set :)

Also... 

Somewhere in the process of fixing the hands, I managed to correct gun aiming at high angles, now if you aim the m16 upwards as if shooting the helicopter, it doesn't bug-out and flip around all wild. Pointing it straight directly up, you may see your gun flip around one way. But this seems to be a rotational issue most shooter VR games face.
